paragraphs.text: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēlthon eis to peran tēs thalassēs eis tēn chōran tōn Gerasēnōn.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come out of the boat, straightway there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ,
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthontos autou ek tou ploiou euthys hypēntēsen autō ek tōn mnēmeiōn anthrōpos en pneumati akathartō,

paragraphs.text: who had his dwelling in the tombs: and no man could any more bind him, no, not with a chain;
paragraphs.original: ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι
paragraphs.translit: hos tēn katoikēsin eichen en tois mnēmasin, kai oude halysei ouketi oudeis edynato auton dēsai

paragraphs.text: because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been rent asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: and no man had strength to tame him.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι·
paragraphs.translit: dia to auton pollakis pedais kai halysesi dedesthai kai diespasthai hypʼ autou tas halyseis kai tas pedas syntetriphthai, kai oudeis ischyen auton damasai·

paragraphs.text: And always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.
paragraphs.translit: kai dia pantos nyktos kai hēmeras en tois mnēmasin kai en tois oresin ēn krazōn kai katakoptōn heauton lithois.

paragraphs.text: And when he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and worshipped him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn ton Iēsoun apo makrothen edramen kai prosekynēsen auton,

paragraphs.text: and crying out with a loud voice, he saith, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I adjure thee by God, torment me not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; ὁρκίζω σε τὸν θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.
paragraphs.translit: kai kraxas phōnē megalē legei· Ti emoi kai soi, Iēsou hyie tou theou tou hypsistou; horkizō se ton theon, mē me basanisēs.

paragraphs.text: For he said unto him, Come forth, thou unclean spirit, out of the man.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: elegen gar autō· Exelthe to pneuma to akatharton ek tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he saith unto him, My name is Legion; for we are many.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Τί ὄνομά σοι; καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōta auton· Ti onoma soi; kai legei autō· Legiōn onoma moi, hoti polloi esmen·

paragraphs.text: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.
paragraphs.translit: kai parekalei auton polla hina mē auta aposteilē exō tēs chōras.

paragraphs.text: Now there was there on the mountain side a great herd of swine feeding.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·
paragraphs.translit: ēn de ekei pros tō orei agelē choirōn megalē boskomenē·

paragraphs.text: And they besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai parekalesan auton legontes· Pempson hēmas eis tous choirous, hina eis autous eiselthōmen.

paragraphs.text: And he gave them leave. And the unclean spirits came out, and entered into the swine: and the herd rushed down the steep into the sea, [in number] about two thousand; and they were drowned in the sea.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epetrepsen autois. kai exelthonta ta pneumata ta akatharta eisēlthon eis tous choirous, kai hōrmēsen hē agelē kata tou krēmnou eis tēn thalassan, hōs dischilioi, kai epnigonto en tē thalassē.

paragraphs.text: And they that fed them fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they came to see what it was that had come to pass.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hoi boskontes autous ephygon kai apēngeilan eis tēn polin kai eis tous agrous· kai ēlthon idein ti estin to gegonos.

paragraphs.text: And they come to Jesus, and behold him that was possessed with demons sitting, clothed and in his right mind, [even] him that had the legion: and they were afraid.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai erchontai pros ton Iēsoun, kai theōrousin ton daimonizomenon kathēmenon himatismenon kai sōphronounta, ton eschēkota ton legiōna, kai ephobēthēsan.

paragraphs.text: And they that saw it declared unto them how it befell him that was possessed with demons, and concerning the swine.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων.
paragraphs.translit: kai diēgēsanto autois hoi idontes pōs egeneto tō daimonizomenō kai peri tōn choirōn.

paragraphs.text: And they began to beseech him to depart from their borders.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto parakalein auton apelthein apo tōn horiōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: And as he was entering into the boat, he that had been possessed with demons besought him that he might be with him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετʼ αὐτοῦ ᾖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai embainontos autou eis to ploion parekalei auton ho daimonistheis hina metʼ autou ē.

paragraphs.text: And he suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go to thy house unto thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and [how] he had mercy on thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς, καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk aphēken auton, alla legei autō· Hypage eis ton oikon sou pros tous sous, kai apangeilon autois hosa ho kyrios soi pepoiēken kai ēleēsen se.

paragraphs.text: And he went his way, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men marvelled.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthen kai ērxato kēryssein en tē Dekapolei hosa epoiēsen autō ho Iēsous, kai pantes ethaumazon.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat unto the other side, a great multitude was gathered unto him; and he was by the sea.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai diaperasantos tou Iēsou en tō ploiō palin eis to peran synēchthē ochlos polys epʼ auton, kai ēn para tēn thalassan.

paragraphs.text: And there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and seeing him, he falleth at his feet,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων, ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ
paragraphs.translit: kai erchetai heis tōn archisynagōgōn, onomati Iairos, kai idōn auton piptei pros tous podas autou

paragraphs.text: and beseecheth him much, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death: [I pray thee], that thou come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be made whole, and live.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει, ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ζήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai parakalei auton polla legōn hoti To thygatrion mou eschatōs echei, hina elthōn epithēs tas cheiras autē hina sōthē kai zēsē.

paragraphs.text: And he went with him; and a great multitude followed him, and they thronged him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthen metʼ autou. Kai ēkolouthei autō ochlos polys, kai synethlibon auton.

paragraphs.text: And a woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years,
paragraphs.original: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος δώδεκα ἔτη
paragraphs.translit: kai gynē ousa en rhysei haimatos dōdeka etē

paragraphs.text: and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρʼ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα,
paragraphs.translit: kai polla pathousa hypo pollōn iatrōn kai dapanēsasa ta parʼ autēs panta kai mēden ōphelētheisa alla mallon eis to cheiron elthousa,

paragraphs.text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came in the crowd behind, and touched his garment.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσασα περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: akousasa peri tou Iēsou, elthousa en tō ochlō opisthen hēpsato tou himatiou autou·

paragraphs.text: For she said, If I touch but his garments, I shall be made whole.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: elegen gar hoti Ean hapsōmai kan tōn himatiōn autou sōthēsomai.

paragraphs.text: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of her plague.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος.
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys exēranthē hē pēgē tou haimatos autēs, kai egnō tō sōmati hoti iatai apo tēs mastigos.

paragraphs.text: And straightway Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power [proceeding] from him had gone forth, turned him about in the crowd, and said, Who touched my garments?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν· Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων;
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys ho Iēsous epignous en heautō tēn ex autou dynamin exelthousan epistrapheis en tō ochlō elegen· Tis mou hēpsato tōn himatiōn;

paragraphs.text: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε, καὶ λέγεις· Τίς μου ἥψατο;
paragraphs.translit: kai elegon autō hoi mathētai autou· Blepeis ton ochlon synthlibonta se, kai legeis· Tis mou hēpsato;

paragraphs.text: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai perieblepeto idein tēn touto poiēsasan.

paragraphs.text: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα, εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν αὐτῇ, ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
paragraphs.translit: hē de gynē phobētheisa kai tremousa, eidyia ho gegonen autē, ēlthen kai prosepesen autō kai eipen autō pasan tēn alētheian.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην, καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autē· Thygatēr, hē pistis sou sesōken se· hypage eis eirēnēn, kai isthi hygiēs apo tēs mastigos sou.

paragraphs.text: While he yet spake, they come from the ruler of the synagogue`s [house] saying, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Teacher any further?
paragraphs.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν· τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον;
paragraphs.translit: Eti autou lalountos erchontai apo tou archisynagōgou legontes hoti Hē thygatēr sou apethanen· ti eti skylleis ton didaskalon;

paragraphs.text: But Jesus, not heeding the word spoken, saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Fear not, only believe.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευε.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous parakousas ton logon laloumenon legei tō archisynagōgō· Mē phobou, monon pisteue.

paragraphs.text: And he suffered no man to follow with him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν οὐδένα μετʼ αὐτοῦ συνακολουθῆσαι εἰ μὴ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰακώβου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk aphēken oudena metʼ autou synakolouthēsai ei mē ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ton adelphon Iakōbou.

paragraphs.text: And they come to the house of the ruler of the synagogue; and he beholdeth a tumult, and [many] weeping and wailing greatly.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου, καὶ θεωρεῖ θόρυβον καὶ κλαίοντας καὶ ἀλαλάζοντας πολλά,
paragraphs.translit: kai erchontai eis ton oikon tou archisynagōgou, kai theōrei thorybon kai klaiontas kai alalazontas polla,

paragraphs.text: And when he was entered in, he saith unto them, Why make ye a tumult, and weep? the child is not dead, but sleepeth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθὼν λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί θορυβεῖσθε καὶ κλαίετε; τὸ παιδίον οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthōn legei autois· Ti thorybeisthe kai klaiete; to paidion ouk apethanen alla katheudei.

paragraphs.text: And they laughed him to scorn. But he, having put them all forth, taketh the father of the child and her mother and them that were with him, and goeth in where the child was.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ. αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκβαλὼν πάντας παραλαμβάνει τὸν πατέρα τοῦ παιδίου καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τοὺς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰσπορεύεται ὅπου ἦν τὸ παιδίον·
paragraphs.translit: kai kategelōn autou. autos de ekbalōn pantas paralambanei ton patera tou paidiou kai tēn mētera kai tous metʼ autou, kai eisporeuetai hopou ēn to paidion·

paragraphs.text: And taking the child by the hand, he saith unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, Arise.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ· Ταλιθα κουμ, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον· Τὸ κοράσιον, σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε.
paragraphs.translit: kai kratēsas tēs cheiros tou paidiou legei autē· Talitha koum, ho estin methermēneuomenon· To korasion, soi legō, egeire.

paragraphs.text: And straightway the damsel rose up, and walked; for she was twelve years old. And they were amazed straightway with a great amazement.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει, ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα. καὶ ἐξέστησαν εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys anestē to korasion kai periepatei, ēn gar etōn dōdeka. kai exestēsan euthys ekstasei megalē.

paragraphs.text: And he charged them much that no man should know this: and he commanded that [something] should be given her to eat.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο, καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai diesteilato autois polla hina mēdeis gnoi touto, kai eipen dothēnai autē phagein.
